study.question: Is the single-seed summary-only full-block permutation penalty concentrated in losing the greatest-index full block at its supplied ordinal location, or is broader coarse rank assignment needed?
study.hypothesis: Local r0086 results show click AUC0.668961270556 supplied,0.668219530812 within-block shuffle,0.665500029457 full-block shuffle, and0.665366790143 both. Coarse summary assignment is more consequential than within-block assignment in these implementations, but the block treatment simultaneously loses endpoint identity and distributed rank. Preserving only the greatest-index full block while shuffling other full blocks may recover more utility than preserving the least-index full block at identical eligible-block count. This is a prospective conditional endpoint hypothesis, not a new architecture claim or established mechanism.

study.proposed_difference: Add a nonlearned moment_block_anchor switch (none/newest/oldest). Only fully occupied ten-slot blocks can move; an anchor excludes one endpoint from the shuffled pool. Build all three maps from the same block priorities in all variants. The two anchor controls have exactly max(F-1,0) eligible blocks per row and no new parameters/buffers. Summary inputs are gathered jointly, and their match union is inversely transported to the unchanged compression view. Four standalone variants differ only in literal CONFIG.
predictions: Implementation: supplied and unrestricted bridges reproduce their r0086 controls; state names/shapes, learned initialization and parameter count match exactly. Invalid positions, full event multisets, task memberships and current targets are preserved.

Mechanism prediction: newest_anchor recovers more of the supplied-minus-unrestricted click-AUC gap than oldest_anchor. Predeclared primary contrast D=AUC(newest)-AUC(oldest), with recovery differences reported in absolute AUC; no unstable ratio if bridge gap is near zero.

Eligibility: anchor arms are identical index treatments for F<=2 and have the same eligible-block count at every F; effective movement is expected for F>=3. Population full-block counts and realized movement must be measured before interpreting the contrast.

A larger direct treatment effect is plausible in histories with more full blocks. Model retraining can also change predictions on untreated/empty rows via shared parameters and Dice state, so those slices need not have identical metrics.

Costs: parameters remain32192421; small nonlearned indexing overhead is expected, but only host-measured allocated GPU seconds, wall time, peak memory and inference throughput/latency determine the cost claim.
falsifiers: An effective equal-eligible-count oldest anchor matches or outperforms newest in the full-population primary score, especially after permitted paired repetition, contradicting special greatest-index endpoint utility in this intervention.
Both anchors failing to recover utility despite adequate F>=3 coverage contradicts sufficiency of retaining one endpoint; it does not refute utility of distributed supplied order.

A null with ineffective movement or few eligible examples cannot falsify the mechanism. Failed event-association, mask, gradient, RNG, bridge or parameter checks invalidate the contrast rather than provide scientific counterevidence.
Evaluation-only sensitivity, a lone favorable seed, auxiliary mean AUC gains, or a source-paper comparison cannot establish the asserted click-utility mechanism.
alternative_explanations: Only the summary view is treated. Compression and within-block order still use supplied order; partial blocks retain ordinal position. This cannot establish that the entire model is order-invariant.

Anchoring reduces the size of the shuffled pool relative to unrestricted shuffling. Only newest-versus-oldest matches that size; both beating unrestricted does not isolate a newest-endpoint mechanism.

The two anchors protect different event contents, target matches, actions, and block-distance distributions. These are part of endpoint information but do not prove a clock-time recency or causal interest-change mechanism.

Shared random priorities couple treatments but do not force equal realized moved counts per example. Measure realized movement and composition; identity draws are valid and must not be redrawn selectively.

Single seed and one training pass can yield optimization, regularization, distribution-shift, and auxiliary-gradient effects. Same-seed identity bridges are execution checks, not independent repetitions.

For F<=2 full blocks both anchor treatments are identity. For F>=3 they remain stochastic and can be identity with probability 1/(F-1)!. Report eligible population and movement before attributing null results.

evidence_review.interpretation: Only successful own-arm validation receipts are supplied here; no local failed execution is concealed or invented. r0084 global random removal and canonical ordering both underperformed supplied order; evaluation-only degradation is sensitivity, not utility evidence. r0085 replacement factorial localized most loss to the summary path rather than compression. r0086 within/block factorial localized a larger decrement to full-block assignment; both interventions was not better than within-only. Canonical and combined-shuffle branches remain negative/unsuccessful trajectories, not erased. The exact supplied-score repetitions are same-seed bridges, not independent support. Existing performance improvements and inherited gradient-engineering lineage do not establish why this topic works.
